title: Calibration of the epicormic 0.1.0 verdict under the null of no provider change

provider.window_salt: request['seed'] + 100000 * replication + 1000 * window_index, applied inside the step callable; window_index 0 is the baseline window, 1..K are the current windows

A1.question: false alarm rate of the window verdict, one baseline window against one current window

A2.question: false alarm rate of the sequential detectors over an EXP-D length horizon

A3.question: the unknown rule fires when every probe is below n_min

run.store: one SQLite pollard store per cell under runs/<run_id>/stores/<part>-p<panel>-n<N>.sqlite; one window per replication and window index, window_id '<part>-r<replication>-w<window_index>'
run.monitor: one monitor per replication, monitor_id '<part>-r<replication>', baseline window index 0, current windows analysed in index order
run.recompute: every verdict is recomputed with analyze over the stored observations before the summary is written; a mismatch fails the run
run.cell_order: A3, A1 in increasing panel size then increasing N, A2; cells are independent and may run in parallel processes

primary.statement: The probability that a null window pair receives the state drift is at most alpha = 0.05 in every A1 cell
primary.test: per cell, the exact one-sided binomial p-value of the drift count of 200 against p0 = 0.05; Holm across the 12 A1 cells at family level 0.05; a cell whose Holm-adjusted p-value is at most 0.05 falsifies the claim for that cell (at the first Holm step this is 20 or more drift verdicts of 200)
primary.report: drift count, warning count, unknown count, rate with two-sided 95 percent Clopper-Pearson interval, raw and Holm-adjusted one-sided p-value, rule_fired breakdown, per cell; the unadjusted per-cell flag of 16 or more drift verdicts of 200 is reported as descriptive; the pooled rate over all 2400 A1 replications with its Clopper-Pearson interval

primary.statement: In the A2 cell the number of replications in which the e-process reaches 1/alpha at any observation within 28 current windows is at most 15 of 200, for each scorer separately and for any scorer
primary.test: exact one-sided binomial test of p <= 0.05 at level 0.05 on the any-scorer count
primary.report: count and rate with Clopper-Pearson interval per scorer and overall; first alarm window distribution; the baseline sample count behind the plug-in rate

secondary.statement: Raw pooled p-values are uniform under the null
secondary.report: per scorer and cell, the empirical fraction of raw pooled p-values at or below 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.50 with Clopper-Pearson intervals, and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance to the uniform distribution; discreteness at N 5 noted

secondary.statement: CUSUM and Page-Hinkley false alarm rates at the default thresholds over 28 windows are reported, not tested
secondary.report: per scorer, the fraction of replications with an alarm within 28 windows, the first alarm window distribution, and the state-level rate of any drift verdict within 28 windows with the rule_fired breakdown

secondary.statement: Every A3 verdict has state unknown with rule 1 fired
secondary.report: count of unknown verdicts of 20; any other state is a defect
fraction of A1 replications with state warning, with the per-probe BH path and the sequential half-threshold path separated

falsification.H-A1: a Holm-adjusted one-sided p-value at or below 0.05 in any A1 cell: the pooled test is anti-conservative at that panel size and N; reported as a defect of epicormic 0.1.0 against the cell, and the paper restricts its calibration claim to the cells that pass
falsification.H-A2: 16 or more replications of 200 with an e-process alarm within 28 null windows: the plug-in baseline rate inflates the false alarm probability at a baseline of 10 samples per probe; reported as the operating characteristic, the paper states the baseline size needed, and the anytime-valid claim is restricted accordingly
falsification.S-A3: any A3 verdict that is not unknown is a defect in the state rules
